messages:
julia: quick check-in — i'm sketching a migration for reducing long-lived API key use. core idea: issue short-lived intent tokens for most flows, keep a tiny admin keyset. thoughts? :thinking:

mike: 👍 makes sense. two quick constraints: (1) metric cardinality (don't tag by token id), (2) mint latency at the edge. can we cache per-principal minted tokens for 1-5m?

sarah: caching is fine but TTLs must be explicit. recommend exp <= 15m by default for service tokens, with a whitelist for offline clients.
cory: ops note — mint service becomes critical infra. need per-tenant throttles, circuit-breaker and an emergency kill-switch. failure modes need to be documented.
julia: agreed. fallback plan: minted -> cached derived-claims (only for read-only, low-risk endpoints) -> deny. derived-claims must be auditable.
mike: how do we preserve lineage for billing and SSO? include a non-secret `parent` claim in minted tokens and surface it to audit logs. avoid putting parent as a high-cardinality metric label.
sarah: RBAC: map claims -> existing role ids via static policy tables. minted tokens carry claims; policy remains stable (no per-token dynamic roles).
cory: migration for external keys: accept legacy keys during rollout, shadow-mint tokens on requests and emit deprecation telemetry. gradually restrict privileges and require rotation.
julia: sample mapping config (pseudo):
```
# rule snippet
when: key: proj-9:abc123
mint: {aud: "svc:inference", claims: ["invoke:model:read"], exp: now + 900, parent: "user:alice@acme"}
```

tammy-bot: canary deploy started for token-slimline experiment: https://deploys.internal/redwood/rollouts/3512 :rocket:

mike: owners? i'll take telemetry + label design. sarah can own policy mapping. cory owns mint-service SLOs & throttles. julia will own RFC draft.
sarah: i'll prepare a short role/claim mapping table and include examples for read vs write routes.
cory: i'll draft failure diagrams and default throttle values. include a runbook for mint outages.
julia: thanks. i'll post an RFC draft with token shapes, claim vocab, migration steps, and metrics (shadow rate, lineage-loss, cardinality) by EOW. ping me if you want included examples.
